newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech c.bank says forex reserves still comfortable.
newsitem.headline: Czech c.bank says forex reserves still comfortable.

text.p: The Czech National Bank said on Wednesday that there were currently just over $3 billion in outstanding Eurobonds denominated in crowns, and that the central bank's reserves were still "several times" that amount.

"About 96.8 billion crowns, or over $3 billion dollars, this is the total amount of (crown) Eurobonds issued now," CNB spokesman Martin Svehla told Reuters. "Our reserves are still several times that amount."
The last official report by the CNB showed the central bank's reserves at $11.718 billion at the end of March virtually unchanged from February.

But that was before a series of interventions by the central bank to buy crowns to halt a slide in the currency last week. Analysts estimate the CNB used between $500 million-$1 billion of its reserves to prop up the currency.
Market analysts have been watching closely the extent to which the central bank will use its precious reserves to defend the crown.
Svehla declined to disclose the extent of the drain on reserves after last week, but said that the level was still comfortable with funds still covering "several months" of imports.
The end-March reserve figure was about 4.5 months of import cover.
In addition to the crown buying, the central bank has raised its last-resort Lombard rate to 50 percent from 14 percent and its repo rate to 45 percent 12.9 to discourage short selling of the crown.
The crown has been under pressure after a series of weak macroeconmic statistics in recent weeks coupled with instability in the centre-right coalition government.
